text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Tiit Vahi offered the Centre Party and Development Party partnership in a coalition and expects an answer today. Vahi plans to present new ministerial candidates to the president tomorrow, the government press service said.
- Companies that are competing for ownership of the chemistry plant KIVITER consider that investments and solutions to environmental problems may be decisive factors in the firm's privatisation.

- Coalition-Centre Party cooperation agreement was not the real reason why the Reform Party left the government. The reformists had plans to came to power after local council elections, Tiit Vahi says in an interview to Postimees.

- Two men who wounded three peeple in a shooting incident at Saturday night were not Defence League members but supporting members and have now been expelled from the organisation, leaders of the Rapla Defence League announced.

- President Lennart Meri will represent Estonia at a OSCE meeting in Lisbon December 2-3. Estonia hopes to sign its border agreement with Russia at the Lisbon meeting, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
- An automatic British radar for controlling aircraft in the Estonian air space will be erected in western Estonia to replace the Russian radar used currently.
- Estonia and Slovenia will sign a free trade agreement in Tallinn on Tuesday.
